summary_paragraphs: Julia mag glamour is a single-location beauty business in Cheverly, MD, operated by sinju Nadia. The account paid for Discovery Agent on 2026-05-11 at $150.00 per month (Discovery-Agent-USD-Monthly SKU). Zoca onboarding occurred 21 days earlier on 2026-04-20 via the Referral lead-source channel. Account executive Krishna Pareek owned the sale; account manager Shruti Sinha owns the post-sale relationship.

Applied against the canonical Module 02 ICP framework, the account fails Step 1.2 (six-month lead-prediction gate) automatically. The model output predicted_6_month_leads = 4 sits 87 percent below the 30-lead Non-ICP floor confirmed by Sales Ops. The internal model further marks nonIcpReason = "Poor Lead Prediction" and triggerReason = "incomplete_data," indicating the predicted-leads figure was itself generated with confidence limited by missing inputs. Module 02's binary rule applies: any single failure in Step 1 or Step 2 = Not ICP. The booking-platform gate (Step 1.3) passes — Julia mag glamour is on Fresha — but a Step-1.3 pass cannot rescue a Step-1.2 automatic fail.

The account also runs into the Module 02 single-location carve-outs at Step 2. The internal categorization model, running against the keyword basket "locs," "twists," "braids near me," "cornrows near me," and "box braid," classified the entity as "Braider." Braiders are one of the four single-location carve-outs explicitly named in Module 02 (alongside threading-only, nails-only, and eyelash-only) at which the cost-to-serve / LTV math does not pencil. BaseSheet's stored primary_category — "Beauty salon," updated to "Hair salon" — does not match the model's read, and the AM must resolve this category-integrity gap before either committing to or refunding the account. If the category resolves to Braider, the carve-out applies and the verdict compounds; if it resolves to general Hair salon or Beauty salon, the carve-out lifts but the Step-1.2 fail still stands.

Reinforcing flags compound the verdict. Module 02 names a < 20 review-count disqualifier; Julia mag glamour sits at 3 reviews at onboarding (despite an exceptional 5.00 average across those three). The Fresha booking-platform URL on file (https://www.fresha.com/lvp/julia-mag-glamour-joyceton-terrace-upper-marlboro-Nyjr6D) was auto-discovered via firecrawl_auto_search on 2026-04-27 against the slug "joyceton-terrace-upper-marlboro" — a different city in Maryland from the BaseSheet locality of Cheverly. The AM should verify this is the same operator and the same shop before treating the platform pass as confirmed.

The Module 02 doctrine for this profile is unambiguous: under the "BE HONEST. FULL STOP." value, account manager Shruti Sinha must contact sinju Nadia within 7 days, run the qualification that was not completed at sale (device, employee count, revenue, Step-2 row, category resolution), and either recover the account cleanly (verified non-braider category AND a real lead pipeline that beats the model projection of 4 AND verified revenue ≥ $100K under solo Rule B) or issue a refund within 14 days and set a re-entry trigger. Given that the lead-prediction figure is in the automatic-fail tier by a wide margin, refund is the most likely Module-02-correct outcome.
exec.net_retention_picture: Account does not meet ICP threshold under Module 02 by a wide margin (predicted leads 4 vs floor 30). Recommended action is AM-led requalification within 7 days, followed by refund within 14 days unless verified facts overturn the model's lead-prediction figure and rule out the Braider carve-out.
exec.likely_outcome: Refund and re-entry trigger. The auto-fail tier on Step 1.2 is decisive; the booking-platform pass cannot rescue it; the carve-out risk at Step 2 (Braider) plus the < 20 reviews disqualifier compound the verdict.

section3_risks.intro: This register catalogues the residual risks associated with allowing this account to remain on Discovery without remediation. The lead-prediction floor is breached by 87 percent (predicted = 4 against a floor of 30), which weights the Day-90 churn risk heavily.

risks.driver_mitigation: Lead-prediction sits at 4 against a floor of 30 — the gap is so wide that even a 5× upside surprise still misses ICP. The model's own nonIcpReason is "Poor Lead Prediction." Mitigation: AM-led requalification + refund-or-recover by Day 14.

Customer paid $150 USD monthly. If churn occurs at Day 90, the at-risk amount is approximately $450 in invoiced revenue plus net cost-to-serve. Mitigation: refund within 14 days bounds the exposure to one to two months of invoiced revenue plus cost-to-serve already incurred.

AE did not ask Step-1.1 (device), did not confirm Step-1.3 (platform — would have passed), did not identify the Step-2 row, did not clarify the category (Braider vs Hair salon), and did not confirm Rule B (revenue). Pattern suggests a fast-close path that bypasses ICP qualification on a Referral lead. Mitigation: Section 7 systemic recommendations.

The model assigned "Braider" (a Module 02 single-location carve-out) using the keyword basket; BaseSheet records "Beauty salon" with updated_primary_category "Hair salon." These cannot both be correct. If Braider, the carve-out applies at Step 2 and compounds the verdict. Mitigation: AM verifies the actual primary service in the first call and updates BaseSheet.

The Fresha booking-platform URL is registered against the slug "joyceton-terrace-upper-marlboro" while BaseSheet records the locality as "Cheverly, MD." Both are in Maryland but are different cities approximately 15 miles apart. The validator cannot rule out cross-entity data conflation. Mitigation: AM identity-verifies the Fresha account in the first call before crediting the Step-1.3 pass.

The model's keyword basket sums to ~275 monthly searches across "locs," "twists," "braids near me," "cornrows near me," and "box braid." Total predicted leads of 4 across six months reflects this thin demand. Mitigation: even with perfect ranking, the underlying demand pool is insufficient. The answer is a refund.

Module 02 disqualifies < 20 reviews at onboarding. Julia mag glamour has 3 reviews. The 5.00 average rating across those three is insufficient compensation; Module 02 requires both a sufficient base AND a strong rating. Mitigation: the review program is a recommended deliverable only if the underlying lead-prediction issue is resolved first.

risks.driver_mitigation: Referral-source customer; if churned without a clean recovery conversation, the referrer relationship is at risk. Mitigation: AM-led honest conversation per Module 02 "BE HONEST. FULL STOP." doctrine; offer refund and re-entry trigger.

section6_actions.intro: Five actions are required to bring this account into Module-02 compliance or to terminate it cleanly with a refund and a re-entry trigger.

actions.action: Call sinju Nadia. Verify operator identity, employee count, category (Braider vs Hair salon vs Beauty salon), Fresha account ownership at the Cheverly shop, and rough annual revenue band. Update BaseSheet category fields accordingly.
actions.success_criterion: AM call notes captured in centralised comms log; BaseSheet primary_category, updated_primary_category, and a free-text note recording employee count and revenue band.

actions.action: Confirm or refute the Step-1.2 lead-prediction figure with sinju Nadia by asking how many net-new client enquiries the shop receives in a typical month right now.
actions.success_criterion: A single number captured: monthly net-new enquiries. If under 5 per month the model is corroborated; if over 10 per month the model is contradicted and the case is escalated to Sales Ops for re-prediction.

actions.action: Decide retain vs refund. Default to refund unless A2 produces a documented enquiry rate that contradicts the model AND A1 produces a category that lifts the carve-out AND Rule B is satisfied.
actions.owner: Shruti Sinha (AM) with Krishna Pareek (AE) consulted
actions.success_criterion: A decision logged in the centralised comms log: "retain (conditions)" or "refund (with re-entry trigger)."

actions.action: Execute the decision. If retain: schedule a 30-day check-in and set a tracked lead-pipeline target. If refund: process the refund through Chargebee and capture the re-entry trigger (the specific event that would qualify this customer in the future).
actions.success_criterion: Chargebee transaction recorded (refund or retained); centralised comms log entry with the next-action timeline.

actions.action: Investigate the one open ticket (BaseSheet open_tickets_last_30_days = 1). Categorise by issue type and resolve before or alongside the recovery call.
actions.success_criterion: Ticket resolved or has an owner with ETA.

section6_actions.am_script: "Hi sinju, this is Shruti from Zoca. Before we go further on Discovery, I want to make sure we set you up right — a couple of quick scope questions. Platform side: I see you're on Fresha — is that the account you actively use, and is that the listing at the Cheverly shop? Services side: when clients book, what are the top two or three services they're asking for? Team — is it just you, or do you have anyone working with you? And finally, monthly enquiries — how many net-new clients reach out in a typical month right now? I'm asking because the model that drives our lead forecasting put your six-month projection at a level that's well below what we typically see for accounts that get value out of Discovery, and I'd rather be straight with you about that today than have you spend $150 a month on something that doesn't fit. Once you answer those four, I can tell you in this call whether we should keep going or whether the honest answer is a refund and a re-entry trigger."
section6_actions.am_script_attribution: Suggested AM opener for Shruti Sinha · 2026-05-11
branch_paragraphs: Branch A — enquiries answer is under 5 per month AND category resolves to braiding-primary: the model and Module 02 agree. Process refund within 14 days; set the re-entry trigger as "open a second location, OR hire your first stylist, OR grow review base past 20."

Branch B — enquiries answer is 5 to 15 per month AND category resolves to general hair / beauty (non-braiding-primary): the model may be undercalling demand. Escalate to Sales Ops for re-prediction with the new category and a fresh lead-volume input. Hold the refund decision pending re-prediction.

Branch C — enquiries answer is over 15 per month: the model is contradicted by lived experience. Document the discrepancy, request manual review by Sales Ops, and consider retaining with a conditional 30-day pipeline target.

section7_systemic.intro: This account exposes systemic gaps that are likely to recur across similarly-shaped accounts. The recommendations below extend beyond Julia mag glamour to the post-sale process as a whole.

recommendations.recommendation: Block first-payment release for accounts whose predicted_6_month_leads is below 30 unless the AE captures a documented contradicting enquiry rate at the point of sale.
recommendations.rationale: Julia mag glamour was allowed to pay at 4 predicted leads — 87 percent below floor. The Module 02 framework is binary at this threshold; the system should enforce it.

recommendations.recommendation: Reconcile BaseSheet primary_category with review_metrics model categorization. When they disagree (as here: Beauty salon / Hair salon vs Braider), surface the conflict as a flag for the AE / AM before sale and as a checked-item in the AM recovery call.
recommendations.rationale: Category integrity drives Step-2 carve-out logic. A silent disagreement between BaseSheet and the model defeats Module 02.

recommendations.recommendation: Add a mandatory Step-2 row identification field to the AE's pre-checkout flow (multi-loc, single+staff, or single+solo). Block checkout if the row is single+solo and the revenue band is not captured.
recommendations.rationale: Step-2 questions were not asked at sale for Julia mag glamour. The Module-02-correct framework requires Step-2 to be answered before payment.

recommendations.recommendation: Populate predicted_6_month_leads into BaseSheet directly. Today it exists in review_metrics but did not sync to BaseSheet for this entity; the validator is reading two sources of truth.
recommendations.rationale: Single source of truth simplifies Module-02 enforcement and avoids silent disagreements between AE-facing and post-sale tooling.

recommendations.recommendation: Wire GBP age into the validator. The gbp.locations CSV is the canonical source; today Julia mag glamour is missing from it.
recommendations.rationale: GBP age < ~3 months is a Module 02 additional disqualifier; it cannot be enforced if the data does not flow.

methodology_paragraphs: This report applies the canonical Module 02 ICP framework (revisions R-05 through R-09, distributed 2026-05-03) to a single Discovery customer that paid at 2026-05-11T10:48:03Z. The framework is binary: any single failure across Step 1 (three hard rules), Step 2 (one matching lead-shape row), or the additional disqualifiers equals Not ICP.

The validator pulls deterministic facts from Chargebee (customer record, subscription, invoice), Metabase BaseSheet (entity-level enrichment), Metabase review_metrics.csv (predicted_6_month_leads, review base, GBP signal), and Metabase booking_platform.csv (Step-1.3 gate). The 5 comms feeds (App Chat, Email, Phone, SMS, Video) were not fetched in this run and are flagged as data gaps where they would otherwise have informed a check. Fireflies and HubSpot were not queried directly.

Statements in this report cite a specific source field for every numerical claim. Where a source could not provide the data required for a Module 02 check, the gap is explicitly flagged (GAP status). No fact is asserted on the basis of inference or external knowledge; only data resident in the listed sources is cited.

qualitative_flags.takeaway: Five of the eight qualitative signals score PASS or GAP — the customer-side signals are clean or unverifiable. The two FAILs (cross-data integrity and demand-side) are structural, not behavioral. The verdict is driven by Module 02 quantitative rules, not by qualitative red flags from the customer.
